gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 1?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecast models indicate a daily maximum near 23–24 °C in Munich on September 1, driven by a stable westerly flow, partly cloudy skies, and light winds under high pressure that limit both warming and cooling. Multiple sources, including WeatherBug, globalmeteo, and Yr.no, converge on highs of 21–24 °C with minimal precipitation risk, aligning closely with the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 22.2 °C. Trader consensus, reflected in the 58.5 % implied probability for 24 °C and 26.5 % for 25 °C, tracks these model outputs without notable shifts in the latest runs. Historical records show extremes ranging from 9.3 °C to 31.8 °C, but present conditions offer little support for outliers. Updated model guidance or surface observations tomorrow morning will be the key data release likely to influence final resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts for Tokyo's maximum temperature on September 1, 2026, center on 28–30 °C, aligning with the market's leading implied probabilities (29 °C at 46%, 28 °C and 30 °C at 23.5% each).** Early September marks the seasonal transition after August's peak, when average daily highs from Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) climatology (1991–2020) hover near 30 °C before declining later in the month.

Current model consensus shows a mostly cloudy to mainly clear pattern with light northeast to east winds, moderate humidity (around 65–80%), and only isolated afternoon showers or drizzle. These conditions limit strong daytime heating while preventing rapid cooling, keeping the daily maximum in a narrow band. Official and private forecasts vary modestly—some project 28–29 °C (e.g., ~84 °F), others up to 31–33 °C—reflecting typical uncertainty in cloud cover and timing of any precipitation.

Trader sentiment therefore concentrates around 29 °C as the most probable single outcome, with nearby values (28 °C and 30 °C) capturing residual model spread. Higher temperatures (31 °C+) carry low odds due to the moderating seasonal baseline and lack of strong southerly flow or clear skies that would support greater insolation. Lower values (27 °C or below) are discounted absent widespread cloud cover or rain suppressing the peak. As the day progresses, updated JMA observations and short-range model runs will refine the exact maximum, which resolves the market based on official Tokyo station data.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent onshore flow and widespread cloud cover with showers are the main drivers capping NYC highs on September 2, 2026, keeping the market tightly balanced between the 74–75°F and 76–77°F bins (each at 30.5% implied probability).** 

Short-range guidance from sources such as WeatherBug and YR.no shows a humid air mass with southeast to east winds of 5–10 mph, extensive cloud cover, and a 60% chance of showers or thunderstorms. These conditions reduce solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling, limiting daytime maxima to the mid- or upper 70s rather than the low 80s that would occur under clearer skies. Model consensus points to peak temperatures occurring midday or early afternoon before additional cloud build-up or rain, producing the narrow range that splits trader bets almost evenly. 

Longer-range seasonal outlooks had hinted at near-normal early-September warmth, but the latest updates emphasize the moderating marine influence and precipitation, explaining why lower bins (72–73°F at 21%) retain meaningful probability while anything above 80°F remains under 4%. Updated NWS or NOAA model runs on September 1–2 will be the key catalyst for any further market movement before resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Historical September 1 averages near 30 °C provide context, but current atmospheric patterns favor the lower end of typical variability.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble forecasts indicate a predominantly westerly airflow across southern England on September 3, with low pressure to the northwest allowing modest warm-air advection from the continent while maintaining cloud cover and scattered light showers. This setup typically produces daytime maxima in the 21–26 °C range, modulated by the precise timing of any breaks in cloud and boundary-layer mixing under 10–15 kt southwesterly winds. Model spreads arise from uncertainties in cloud thickness and frontal timing, which can alter peak insolation by several degrees. Historical early-September climatology for London shows a mean daily maximum near 20–22 °C, so current guidance sits slightly above average yet well below heatwave thresholds, explaining the broad, evenly matched market-implied probabilities across the mid-20s. Updated high-resolution runs and Met Office briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely narrow the range.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Persistent cloud cover, light southerly flow, and scattered showers kept temperatures below the 81°F climatological average, with hourly readings peaking near 78°F before cooling. This outcome aligns with model consensus from the prior weekend showing suppressed insolation and modest marine influence. While final quality-controlled data releases could theoretically shift a single station reading by 1°F, the multi-site agreement makes such revisions improbable.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecast consensus from numerical weather models and observational data strongly supports a Tokyo maximum of 28°C on September 1, 2026, reflected in the market's 97% implied probability on that outcome.** Persistent cloud cover, light northeasterly to easterly flow, and modest moisture (with isolated drizzle possible) are limiting daytime solar heating and keeping surface temperatures in check, consistent with GFS, regional guidance, and real-time reports showing afternoon readings peaking near 28–29°C (roughly 82–84°F) under mostly cloudy skies.

This positioning aligns with early-September climatology for the Tokyo observation site, where transitional post-summer patterns often cap highs around the upper 20s°C when subtropical ridging weakens and marine influence increases. Historical baselines from the Japan Meteorological Agency place early-September maxima near 28–30°C on average, and today's conditions match the lower end of that range due to reduced insolation rather than an anomalous cool outbreak.

Realistic challenges to the 28°C consensus would require unexpected clearing that boosts insolation enough to add 1–2°C, or a shift in steering flow allowing warmer air advection—scenarios models currently assign low probability but that could be tested by afternoon satellite and surface observations. Higher outcomes (29°C+) carry only 3% combined market weight, underscoring trader confidence in the stable, suppressed thermal profile.
